headline: BTC closed below its 200-day average; long funding jumped from 3% back to 10% in a day, and short-term holders sold at a loss 1.4× September's level.
summary: Breaking the 200-day average did not flush leverage: perp open interest rose 13,000 BTC in a day and longs are paying 10% funding again. Short-term holders realized 40% more loss than at the September low, and only 23% of their coins are in profit. The plan hedges only after 5 closes below 73,082; today is day 1. PPI and the Deribit weekly expiry land on Friday.

overview.lead: The break of the 200-day average came at peak selling: short-term holders are capitulating while leverage is adding, and both forces were in the market today.
points: Close 71,371, down 3.5% on 1.6× the 20-day average volume; it closed near the day's low with no late bid.
Sellers were short-term holders: realized loss 5,874 BTC versus realized profit of only 2,425 BTC (CheckOnChain, Nov 12).
Part of the buying was leverage: three-venue funding 3.1% → 10.3%, open interest 351,132 BTC, 99th percentile since 2021.
ETFs lost $309M on Nov 11, the 5th straight outflow day, $1.49B over the 5 days.

cycle.lead: The market stage is still bull, day 35: it only reverts to bear after 30 straight closes below a falling 200-day average, and the average is still rising.
points: 2 of 6 supporting lights are on: capital inflow (realized cap +0.15% over 30 days) and exchange supply, which just turned on (−0.3% over 90 days); 12-month momentum, MVRV vs its 1-year mean, short-term holder cost and STH cost vs true market mean are off.
Dawn Index heat 33.6, week 9 of Daybreak; the weekly bull–bear score is 0.32, week 7 of early bull; neither has turned (Nov 11).
Tidemark bottom signal 28.4, outside its bottom zone; its cycle-low test runs to Dec 19 and fails on a break of the Jun 30 low at 58,525.
At the last 30 days' pace, a straight-line extrapolation puts the short-term holder cost crossing above the true market mean near Jan 2, 2027.

market.lead: Sell Pressure Index at 100 with momentum 0.17: the bottom combination is on day 3, but this leg is down 17.6% over 52 days from 86,594 with no bounce yet.
points: The bottom combination has fired 20 times since 2012; 30 days later price was higher 11 times, median +1.8%, below the +3.2% of any day; after Aug 2014 and May 2022 it fell another 40%+.
The close is below the 5-, 10- and 20-day averages and at 0% of the 20-day range, the lowest close in 20 days.
1-year position is the 38th percentile, 11% above the q10 line at 63,547.

deriv.lead: Price down, leverage up: longs re-entered below the 200-day average, and the estimated long liquidation band below is almost 5× thicker than above.
points: This section's finding is open interest up 13,000 BTC in a day; the same day perp takers sold 15,259 BTC more than they bought, so some new positions are shorts, but funding back at 10% says longs are willing to pay again.
Estimated long liquidation bands sit at 69.9–71.0K (1.4% below the close) and 66.8–69.8K (4.4% below); within 5% of the close, 42,859 BTC is estimated below versus 9,174 BTC above.
The Nov 13 Deribit weekly holds 9.3% of open interest, max pain 76,000; DVOL 40.1, with 7- and 90-day implied vol both at 38–39% and a flat curve.
The largest bid wall is $177M at 70,000 and the largest ask wall $208M at 71,000, both on Hyperliquid perps.

flows.lead: Dollars are still leaving, mostly through ETFs today: 5 straight outflow days and −$1.92B over 20 trading days, this year's fifth deep outflow stretch.
points: ETFs −$309M on Nov 11 (CoinMarketCap; Farside via media: −$299.8M), IBIT out 9 sessions in a row; Nov 12 is not out yet.
The close is 9.6% below the estimated ETF holder cost basis (ex-GBTC).

Stablecoins $289.1B, −1.5% over 7 days and −$14.9B over 30; the Coinbase premium net of USDT averages −0.008% over 7 days, near zero, while the USDT discount (7-day −0.13%) is still in the lowest 5% of four years.
Polymarket prices a December hike at 97.7%; the 2-year yield is 4.86%, 0.86 points above the Fed's upper bound.

onchain.lead: Short-term holders are capitulating: loss-taking is 40% larger than at the September low and only 23% of their coins are in profit, while long-term holders have not sped up.
points: Two findings here: concentrated short-term holder loss-taking on day 3 (loss z-score 4.2), and 560K BTC changed price levels in a week, 80% of it moved at a loss.
Long-term holder 7-day realized loss is $1.4B with LTH-SOPR at 0.955; the long-term holder loss share is 35.7%, far from 45.4% on Jun 30.
Apparent demand is −290K BTC over 30 days, below its own 30-day average; Nov 22 is the echo of last year's suspected wallet move, so a sharp drop around then is not read as weaker demand.
7-day hashrate 938 EH/s, −9.6% in a week; the Nov 13 difficulty adjustment is estimated at −7.8%.

exit.lead: No exit rule has fired; the only nearby action point is the 200-day average, and today is the first close below it.
points: Hedge rule: 5 straight closes below the 200-day average at 73,082 → cut 20%, earliest on the Nov 16 close; buy back after 5 closes above it or a 7-day MVRV Z below 0.5.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak is 0.49, far from the 0.75 line (112,188); the three top indicators read 30 / 26 / 37, all low (Nov 11).

news.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately and the stock fell as much as 14% intraday; BTC dropped to about 71,200, a near 12-week low
news.read: Tech-stock risk passed straight into BTC: the 30-day BTC–Nasdaq correlation is 0.70, and the close below the 200-day average came on this day. Nasdaq closed only −0.39% while BTC fell 3.5%, with leveraged longs as the amplifier. This is a short-term shock; the cycle read depends on whether the 200-day average is reclaimed within 5 days.

news.title: Spot BTC ETFs saw $299.8M net outflows on Nov 11, a 5th straight day; IBIT lost $269.7M, its 9th straight session
news.read: Same direction as this site's CoinMarketCap figure of −$309M; SoSoValue shows −$299.9M. The 20-day total is −$1.92B, past the −$1.5B outflow-stretch line; earlier stretches bottomed at −$4.7B and −$5.6B, so this one is still shallow. As long as outflows continue, US spot demand has not returned.

news.title: San Francisco Fed's Daly said further tightening will be needed; the 2-year yield rose 7bp to 4.80%
news.read: Fed officials are openly discussing hikes, and Polymarket's December hike odds reached 97.7% (78.2% a week ago). The 2-year sits 0.86 points above the policy upper bound, so bonds already price hikes; for BTC it is a rising cost-of-money backdrop that does not by itself decide the cycle.

news.title: The US 10-year yield rose to about 5.10% and gold fell 2.8% to $3,876 an ounce
news.read: Gold and BTC fell on the same day: the selling hit every asset that pays no yield; over two months gold (PAXG) is −10.9% and BTC −7.6%. With yields above 5%, the pressure on non-yielding assets is not BTC-specific.

news.title: US initial jobless claims 200K versus 195K expected; October existing-home sales at a 3.75M annual rate, the lowest since August 2010
news.read: Housing is frozen under high rates while jobs have not clearly weakened, so the Fed has no reason to stop. A hot PPI on Friday would only firm up the hike; for BTC it is background and does not change the cycle read on its own.

news.title: Houthis claimed attacks on a Saudi East-West pipeline station and a Yanbu facility; Brent rose 3.3% to settle at $95.82
news.read: Higher oil lifts inflation expectations and yields together, one more reason to hike. Iran's claim that 4 tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz could not be verified by Reuters (unverified); Brent is still down about 2.5% on the week, so this is not a new oil shock yet.

news.title: BTC options expiring on Deribit Nov 13 total about $2.48B notional, max pain 76,000, put/call 0.52
news.read: This site reads the same expiry at 33,367 BTC, 9.3% of open interest, max pain 76,000, 6.5% above the close; it is small, and the big positions sit in Nov 27 and Dec 25. Open interest does not show who is long or short, so heavy calls do not mean bullish.

news.title: The next difficulty adjustment is projected at −6.4% to −7.8%, the largest cut since June; 7-day hashrate fell below 1 ZH/s
news.read: This site reads 7-day hashrate at 938 EH/s via mempool.space, −9.6% in a week, an estimated −7.8% adjustment and hashprice at $34.5. Miner revenue is shrinking and machines are switching off, but Hash Ribbons have not flipped to capitulation (30-day average still above the 60-day).

news.title: The US DOJ won court approval to seize $1.2B tied to the Binance hack, attributed to North Korea's TraderTraitor; more than $2.7B is frozen in total
news.read: Frozen and recovered funds reduce the risk of hackers dumping coins on the market; Binance has set aside $6.34B to cover losses. It is unrelated to today's on-chain selling and has no bearing on the cycle read.

findings.title: The 200-day break didn't flush leverage: open interest rose 13,000 BTC in a day
findings.lean_why: Longs are adding into the decline and paying high funding, and estimated liquidations below outweigh those above, so another drop could be amplified by forced selling.
findings.what: Leverage came back on a day price fell 3.5%: perp open interest went 338,130 → 351,132 BTC and three-venue funding 3.1% → 10.3% (Coinalyze, exchanges, Nov 12). Yesterday we wrote that longs left on their own; correction today: funding was back at 10% within a day.
findings.why: By venue, OKX and Hyperliquid funding both reached 11% and Binance 9.8%, so it is not one exchange. Open interest is in the 99th percentile since 2021 and +14.8% over 30 days while price is −14.1%; 72.6% of Binance accounts are long, 92nd percentile. But perp takers sold 15,259 BTC more than they bought in the day, and the top 2,000 Hyperliquid accounts are net short 12.3K BTC versus 7.8K long, so not all new positions are longs. On spot, Coinbase takers sold 4,819 BTC more than they bought over 7 days, 2nd percentile in four years, so spot buying did not follow.
findings.alt: Some of the new open interest may be basis trades or short hedges, and higher funding could also come from shorts closing and lifting the perp price; Coinalyze's daily open interest and funding are closing snapshots that miss intraday moves. The liquidation bands are estimates built on assumed leverage.
findings.history: Days with more than 72% of accounts long occurred 26 times in the past year; 90 days later price was higher only 10 times, median −7% (any day: 53% higher). The overheated zone of a 7-day funding average above 30% is not in play; it is 7.5% now, 61st percentile since 2021.
findings.so: With leverage intact, the fuel for a further drop is still there: 42,859 BTC of estimated liquidations within 5% below the close versus 9,174 BTC above. The market stage and the exit plan have not moved.
findings.next: Over the next week, watch open interest. A drop below 330K BTC would mean leverage has left and refutes this; 7-day long liquidations above $800M would mean the cascade has started, confirming it.

findings.title: Short-term holders are capitulating, selling at a loss 40% more than at the September low
findings.lean_why: Rising loss-taking is fresh supply short term; capitulation like this has usually come late in declines, but often not for the last time.
findings.what: Short-term holders are capitulating: realized loss 5,874 BTC, 2.4× the 2,425 BTC of realized profit, and only 23% of short-term supply is in profit (CheckOnChain, Bitview, Nov 12).
findings.why: Losses are doing the work: versus 7 days ago, realized profit is −43% and realized loss +54%. The network-wide loss peak is 7.57bp of market cap versus 5.41bp at the Sep 15 low, a lower price with bigger loss-taking. The short-term holder loss z-score is 4.2, above 2 for 3 days; STH-SOPR is 0.983, below 1 for 7 days and deeper than the Oct 30 low of 0.992. Outside data agree: CryptoQuant counted about 47K BTC sent to exchanges at a loss on Nov 11. Long-term holders have not sped up: their 7-day realized loss is $1.4B versus $3.6B at the Jun 30 low.
findings.alt: Everything here is per-UTXO, so exchange wallet consolidation counts as loss-taking too; CheckOnChain data are smoothed and about 1 day late. The loss peak is unconfirmed (it needs 7 days on each side); if price falls further the peak grows, so 7.57 may not be the top of this leg.
findings.history: Lower price with bigger loss-taking has appeared 58 times since 2013; 30 days later price was higher 44 times, median +6.9%. Concentrated short-term holder loss-taking below the 200-day average happened 23 times, higher 30 days later 10 times, median −0.8%, about the same as any day under that condition. The SPI 100 plus momentum 0.17 bottom combination is on day 3; of 20 cases, 11 were higher 30 days later.
findings.so: The sellers in this leg are short-term holders; long-term holders have not joined, so the joint capitulation seen at the late-June bottom has not happened yet. The exit plan watches the 200-day average only, so this finding does not move it.
findings.next: Within a week, watch for another wave: short-term holder realized loss above 7,000 BTC means capitulation is widening; the loss z-score back below 2 means this wave is over.

findings.title: 560K BTC moved to 71–74K in a week, mostly at a loss; new cost basis sits just above price
findings.lean_why: Freshly moved coins have a cost above the current price, so every bounce to 73–74K meets holders looking to break even.
findings.what: This week's buying sat just above today's price: URPD shows 560K BTC moved out of their price levels over 7 days, 450K of it from coins whose cost was above the week's high; the biggest gains were the 73K, 71K and 74K buckets (Bitview, Nov 12).
findings.why: The question is whose cost sits above and below once 72K broke. Above: the largest outflows were from 80K (−143K BTC), 77K and 76K, into 71–74K; the 71,371 close is at the bottom of those buckets, so the new coins went underwater right away. Short-term holder cost is 75,429 and the thickest short-term bucket is 76K (493K BTC, CheckOnChain). Below: at 70K, 73% of short-term supply would be underwater, at 64K 84%, at 62K 97% (CheckOnChain actual coin age); the next thick layer is still 62–66K. In behavior, the jump in short-term realized loss matches the 450K BTC moved at a loss; but ETFs were out 5 days running, so the buyers were not US spot.
findings.alt: On-chain moves are not necessarily trades, and exchange housekeeping can shift coins between price levels; URPD lags about 1 day, and the $1,000 bucket grid affects which bucket looks thickest. The 71K bucket, now the thickest at 253K BTC, could also act as support.
findings.history: This is a structural reading with no ready-made backtest; the related call was Nov 10's "thin supply from 72K to 66K", confirmed today by the close below 72K.
findings.so: Sellers have handed coins to this week's 71–74K buyers, so 73–74K has turned from support into those buyers' break-even level; the thick 62–66K layer has not been tested, so support below remains unproven.
findings.next: Within a week, a close back above 74K puts the new coins in profit and refutes this; short-term supply in profit below 20% means even the 71K layer is trapped, confirming it.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Running on Empty
items.points: BTC near 74K, below short-term holder cost of 75.6K, with only about 35% of short-term supply in profit; true market mean 77.5K; two-thirds of short-term supply sits above price, and the only thick layer below is 62–66K. Stablecoins shrank $14.2B in 30 days; the largest long liquidation band is 59.5–62.6K; holding the June low at 58.5K keeps August's trend reversal intact.
items.meaning: Today's close is 71,371 and this site reads 23% of short-term supply in profit, well below its 35%; 62–66K is still the only thick layer below (see 2026-11-12-3).

items.title: Bitcoin: Correction or Reset?
items.points: Via media coverage: short-term holder cost 75,717, with BTC below it for 4 days; reclaiming it plus 3 straight ETF inflow days would mark a correction, otherwise a reset; 11 of 14 past breaks were reclaimed within two weeks. Futures open interest 701.9K BTC, up 3.3% while price fell, funding about 11% annualized.
